description: Telemetry profiles referenced by rule sidecars. Each profile documents the logsource, channels, fields, prerequisites, and known collection gaps for a family of rules.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
win_process_creation.retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.

collection_prerequisites: Registry value-set auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 13 or equivalent).
The autostart hives of interest are included in the collection filter.
expected_collection_gaps: Registry auditing is frequently filtered to a small key allowlist.
Values written by offline hive edits are not observed.
normalization_assumptions: TargetObject uses the full registry path with HKLM or HKU prefixes.
Details contains the written value rendered as text.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines split TargetObject into key and value name fields.
REG_BINARY values may be rendered differently between agents.
win_registry_set.retention_considerations: Registry value telemetry is moderate volume; 90 days is usually affordable.

collection_prerequisites: File creation auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent).
User-writable directories are not globally excluded from collection.
expected_collection_gaps: File modification without creation may not raise an event.
Aggressive exclusion lists commonly remove temporary directories.
normalization_assumptions: TargetFilename is an absolute path including the file extension.
Image identifies the writing process.
ingestion_differences: Some agents report short paths or device paths instead of drive letters.
Extension casing varies between producers.
win_file_event.retention_considerations: File creation telemetry is high volume; 30 days of hot retention is typical.

collection_prerequisites: Process access auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 10 or an EDR equivalent).
The sensitive authentication process is included in the monitored target list.
expected_collection_gaps: Process access auditing is often disabled because of its volume.
Kernel-mode access paths are not represented in this event class.
normalization_assumptions: GrantedAccess is a hexadecimal string such as 0x1010.
SourceImage and TargetImage are absolute paths.
ingestion_differences: Some producers emit GrantedAccess as a decimal integer.
CallTrace availability depends on symbol resolution settings.
win_process_access.retention_considerations: Process access telemetry is very high volume; scope filters are required.

collection_prerequisites: WMI subscription auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event IDs 19, 20 and 21).
The agent configuration does not exclude WMI activity generated by management tools.
expected_collection_gaps: Subscriptions created before agent deployment are not observed.
Remote subscription creation may be attributed to the target host only.
normalization_assumptions: EventType distinguishes filter, consumer, and binding records.
Operation is either Created or Deleted.
ingestion_differences: Field names differ between Sysmon and WMI-Activity operational logs.
Query text may be truncated by some pipelines.
win_wmi_event.retention_considerations: WMI subscription telemetry is low volume and inexpensive to retain for a year.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
win_security.retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.

collection_prerequisites: The System event log is collected from endpoints and servers.
Service Control Manager events are not filtered out by the forwarder subscription.
expected_collection_gaps: Service installation performed by driver loading is not represented here.
Servers with aggressive System log filters may drop Event ID 7045.
normalization_assumptions: ImagePath contains the full service binary path including any arguments.
Provider_Name identifies Service Control Manager.
ingestion_differences: Quoted service paths may or may not retain surrounding quotation marks.
Some pipelines rename ImagePath to service.executable.
win_system.retention_considerations: System log volume is low; 365 days of retention is generally affordable.

collection_prerequisites: Script block logging is enabled through Group Policy or registry configuration.
PowerShell operational log collection is enabled on the endpoint.
expected_collection_gaps: PowerShell version 2 engines do not emit script block logs.
Very large script blocks are split across multiple events.
normalization_assumptions: ScriptBlockText contains the decoded script text as executed.
EventID 4104 identifies script block execution.
ingestion_differences: Multi-part script blocks may need reassembly before matching.
Some pipelines strip newlines from ScriptBlockText.
win_ps_script.retention_considerations: Script block logging is moderate to high volume; 90 days is a common target.

collection_prerequisites: An execve audit rule or equivalent process telemetry agent is deployed.
Audit rules are not limited to a narrow allowlist of binaries.
expected_collection_gaps: Containers without a shared audit namespace may not report execve records.
Audit backlog limits can drop records under load.
normalization_assumptions: Image is the absolute executable path and CommandLine is the joined argument vector.
ParentImage identifies the parent executable path.
ingestion_differences: auditd argument vectors may be hex-encoded before normalization.
Some agents report the argv array instead of a joined string.
linux_process_creation.retention_considerations: Execve telemetry is high volume; 30 to 60 days of hot retention is typical.

collection_prerequisites: Audit watch rules cover the sensitive directories referenced by the rule.
The audit daemon is running and its rules survive reboot.
expected_collection_gaps: Directories without an explicit watch rule produce no events.
Bind-mounted paths inside containers may bypass host watches.
normalization_assumptions: TargetFilename is an absolute POSIX path.
Image identifies the writing process where the producer supplies it.
ingestion_differences: Path reconstruction from auditd PATH records varies between agents.
Relative paths may appear when the working directory record is missing.
linux_file_event.retention_considerations: File watch telemetry is moderate volume; 90 days is a reasonable target.

collection_prerequisites: The authentication facility is forwarded from the host to the collector.
The syslog message body is preserved rather than truncated.
expected_collection_gaps: Hosts using journald without syslog forwarding require a different collector.
Rate-limited syslog can drop bursts of failures.
normalization_assumptions: ProcessName holds the syslog program name and Message holds the free-text body.
SourceIp is populated only for network authentication attempts.
ingestion_differences: Distribution-specific message wording differs between sshd builds.
Some pipelines pre-parse the message into structured fields.
linux_auth.retention_considerations: Authentication logs are low volume; 365 days of retention is common.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.OriginalFileName: Original file name recorded in the binary version resource.
field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.
field_semantics.ParentImage: Absolute path of the executable that created the process.
field_semantics.ParentCommandLine: Command line of the creating process.
field_semantics.CurrentDirectory: Working directory of the created process.
field_semantics.User: Account context in which the event was produced.
field_semantics.Computer: Host on which the event was produced.
field_semantics.Channel: Windows event log channel that carried the record.
field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.Provider_Name: Name of the event provider that raised the record.
field_semantics.TargetObject: Full registry path of the value that was written.
field_semantics.Details: Rendered data written to the registry value.
field_semantics.EventType: Sub-type of the telemetry record, such as SetValue or WmiBindingEvent.
field_semantics.TargetFilename: Absolute path of the file that was created or modified.
field_semantics.SourceImage: Absolute path of the process requesting access.
field_semantics.TargetImage: Absolute path of the process being accessed.
field_semantics.GrantedAccess: Hexadecimal access mask granted for the process handle.
field_semantics.CallTrace: Call stack recorded for the access request where available.
field_semantics.Operation: Lifecycle operation applied to the subscription component.
field_semantics.Name: Name of the subscription component.
field_semantics.Query: Query text associated with the event filter.
field_semantics.ServiceName: Name of the service registered with the service control manager.
field_semantics.ImagePath: Executable path configured for the service, including arguments.
field_semantics.ServiceType: Service type reported at installation time.
field_semantics.StartType: Configured start type of the service.
field_semantics.AccountName: Account under which the service is configured to run.
field_semantics.ScriptBlockText: Decoded PowerShell script block text as executed.
field_semantics.ScriptBlockId: Identifier grouping the parts of a single script block.
field_semantics.Path: Script file path when the script block originates from a file.
field_semantics.SubjectUserName: Account that performed the audited action.
field_semantics.SubjectDomainName: Domain of the account that performed the audited action.
field_semantics.TargetUserName: Account or group that was the object of the audited action.
field_semantics.TargetDomainName: Domain of the object of the audited action.
field_semantics.MemberName: Distinguished name or account name of the affected group member.
field_semantics.IpAddress: Network address associated with the authentication attempt.
field_semantics.TaskName: Full path of the scheduled task in the task library.
field_semantics.TaskContent: Serialised task definition including trigger and action elements.
field_semantics.ObjectDN: Distinguished name of the directory object involved in the operation.
field_semantics.AttributeLDAPDisplayName: Directory attribute affected by the change.
field_semantics.AttributeValue: Value written to the directory attribute.
field_semantics.OperationType: Type of directory modification, such as value added or deleted.
field_semantics.Properties: Directory attributes or property sets touched by the access request.
field_semantics.AuditPolicyChanges: Description of the audit subcategory settings that changed.
field_semantics.CategoryId: Audit policy category affected by the change.
field_semantics.SubcategoryId: Audit policy subcategory affected by the change.
field_semantics.ProcessName: Program name recorded by the system logger.
field_semantics.Message: Free-text message body recorded by the system logger.
field_semantics.SourceIp: Network address of the remote authentication client.
field_semantics.Mode: File permission mode recorded for the affected path.
